thread:
jin: Heads-up — saw a sharp memory cliff on prod-2 during mixed-length traffic around 09:10. Multiple OOMs but only after a compaction pass finished. Suspect: thinband fragmentation in the block pool after aggressive coalescing.

jin: snippet from dmesg / runtime logs: ```
[2025-07-12T09:10:34Z] OOM: gpu_alloc failed alloc_bytes=10485760 pool=blockpool
[2025-07-12T09:10:34Z] blockpool: compaction finished, freed=1.2MB, fragments=127
[2025-07-12T09:10:34Z] workspace_resize: old=512K new=1.5M reason=kv-cache-reuse
[2025-07-12T09:10:34Z] allocator: split small-block idx=42 size=384->256+128
```

mike: can you attach the perf counters (allocation rate, free list churn, queued_batches) from the trace?

jin: quick paste from perf-client: `alloc_s/s=1220 free_s/s=1187 freelist_hits=0.37 queued_batches=6 avg_seq=192`

sara: queued_batches=6 is the kicker — compaction was triggered while multiple batches were inflight. When compaction coalesces heterogeneous small blocks we end up with many tiny fragments that later force splits during workspace_resize. That spike is what pushes us over the cliff.

omar: idea: throttle background compaction if queued_batches > compaction_threshold (default 4). Also consider prioritizing coalescing of blocks with matching seqlen histograms to avoid thinband fragmentation.

mike: +1. Another quick experiment: disable thinband coalescing for blocks < 512 bytes (cheap to keep them separate) and prefer reuse of contiguous-run blocks for KV cache hits. Might reduce fragmentation at cost of slightly higher peak memory.

jin: ran a local repro with both changes: disabling tiny-coalesce stopped the OOMs but increased P95 token latency by ~8% under heavy tail workloads. Numbers: baseline mem-peak=21.4GB, patched mem-peak=20.9GB, tail-latency +8%.

lucy: if latency regresses, maybe we can do a hybrid: keep tiny-coalesce disabled only when queued_batches > 3 or when recent compaction freed < X bytes. Essentially a guard that looks at both inflight load and compaction effectiveness.

mike: could also add a reuse-hint to the allocator API: callers (attention kernel) can indicate "prefer same-seqlen" for blocks allocated for KV caches. Then blockmgr can bias reuse rather than blind coalescing. Low-effort, high-value for page attention patterns.

jin: prototype of config flags I used: ```json
{
  "compaction": {"enable_thinband_coalesce": false, "min_coalesce_size": 512, "throttle_if_queued_batches_gt": 3},
  "allocator": {"reuse_hint_seqlen_match": true}
}
```

sara: plan: 1) run canary 5% with the guard (throttle+min_coalesce=512), 2) collect P95/P99 and mem-peak and freelist_hit rate, 3) if P95 delta < 5% and mem-peak improved, roll to 25%.

omar: add tracing hook to record "compaction_effectiveness": freed_bytes / scanned_bytes per pass. That will help tune the min_coalesce threshold empirically.

jin: noted. I'll attach repro script and perf dashboards to the PR. Thanks all — will post updates once canary data is in. :thumbsup:
